basics.name: Dwight Doane
basics.label: Frontend && Full-Stack Engineer
basics.summary: I like knowing how things work, which is how I got into reverse engineering web apps and building my own dev tools. That's taken me through more than a decade on the web, mostly in Elm, from live streaming to compliance software. Along the way I've taught bootcamp students, brought plenty of engineers into functional programming, and started building tools for AI agents.

work.summary: Full-stack work on Avetta's supplier compliance platform: a large production Elm frontend talking to Scala services.
highlights: Owned creator filtering for Worksite Safety from start to finish. Broke the epic into a ticket per service, then built all of them: the Elm filter UI on four list and calendar views, a new Scala 3 aggregation service (http4s/Tapir), and the Play/MongoDB storage behind it
Worked on the formula builder in our forms configuration tool, which lets configuration engineers write, save, and test scoring formulas themselves instead of waiting on an engineer
Built the settings screens client admins use to manage review chains, including the unglamorous parts: reset to defaults, clear all, and deletes that explain themselves when the server says no
Built an in-app Elm inspector for the team. Point at anything on the page and it tells you which view function rendered it, and on what line
Left 400+ review comments across 180+ PRs, and turned about 3,400 past review comments from across the org into Elm and Scala style guides the team now reviews against

work.summary: Kicked off and architected the rewrite of CareRev's facility app from React to Elm. The app helped hospitals find and book qualified nurses.
highlights: Got engineers of every level productive in Elm, from juniors to seniors new to functional programming, and wrote the team's Elm conventions
Shipped Smart Rates and other features that saved large hospital clients time and money
Built a design system in Tailwind with our designers, plus a Storybook so everyone could see and reuse the pieces
Wrote codegen scripts to handle tedious work, like keeping Amplitude tracking in sync with the tracking plan
Interviewed candidates and wrote the code challenges we hired with

work.summary: Rebuilt Halogen, our live streaming platform, inside Triller after they acquired it.
highlights: Artists like Jennifer Lopez and DJ Khaled used our scheduled and live streaming tools to perform for thousands of fans
Our platform hosted the Verzuz battle series, where viewers voted on who was winning in real time

work.summary: Built Halogen, a live streaming platform for artists and creators, in Elm, JavaScript, and Web Components.
highlights: Grew it past 120k lines of Elm before Triller acquired it
Built the interactive side of a stream: tipping, gifting, chat, and live and prerecorded playback
Helped move the app from Elm 0.18 to 0.19, and from BEM-style CSS to Tailwind
Taught incoming React engineers Elm and functional programming
Built responsive layouts so fans could watch on a phone or a desktop

work.summary: Helped rewrite an aging PHP app in React and Redux (redux-observable, redux-saga).
Taught web development to bootcamp students, from HTML and CSS through Node, React, and databases. Filled in as instructor, graded homework, and helped students in class and online.
highlights: Ran extra sessions on things the curriculum skipped, like ES6, functional programming, and Git basics
Found out here how much I like teaching and mentoring

work.summary: Built frontend apps with designers, DBAs, and stakeholders, including gogreenback.com.
highlights: Built gogreenback's web app in Angular.js, plus the webviews inside its iOS and Android apps

projects.name: Ternpike
projects.summary: A local-first trip expense tracker written in Elm. Snap a receipt and Claude fills in the expense, with your data stored on your device first.

projects.name: Snapkin
projects.summary: Calipers in, CAD out. Photograph each face of a part, tap two edges, enter your caliper reading, and Snapkin exports the dimensions for Fusion.

projects.name: Sandlot Derby
projects.summary: A minimalist home run derby for iOS. Swipe through the pitch to swing: the direction sets the angle, the speed sets the power, and the ball flies with real air drag. Prototyped in the browser first, then built on a tested pure-Swift physics core.

projects.name: resq
projects.summary: A command-line tool for reading and editing ReScript code, designed for AI agents first. An agent can pull out one function instead of a whole file, and a bad edit never leaves the file half-changed. Ported from elmq.

projects.name: rewind
projects.summary: An Elm-style time-travel debugger for ReScript React apps. Pause a running app, step back through every message and model, see exactly what changed, and export the history as JSON.

projects.name: elm-peek
projects.summary: A browser extension that adds go-to-definition for Elm code on GitHub, and warns you when a pull request adds a new variant that some case expression will quietly ignore.

projects.name: elm-view-name-injector
projects.summary: A build step that tags every element on the page with the Elm view function that drew it, so people and AI agents can go straight from the screen to the code.

projects.name: elm-storybook-verify-examples
projects.summary: Combines Ryan Haskell-Glatz's Elm Storybook setup with elm-verify-examples, so the examples in your doc comments become Storybook stories automatically. One example works as documentation, a test, and a live component preview.

projects.name: pr-digest
projects.summary: A command-line tool and macOS menu bar plugin that shows the pull requests waiting on you, and flags anything new since you last looked.

projects.name: munbyn-print
projects.summary: Prints to a Munbyn thermal label printer over USB or Bluetooth without the vendor's driver, which doesn't run on Apple Silicon. Speaks the printer's own command language and works around firmware quirks I found by testing on the real hardware.
